text:
## Abstract  
We investigated how many raw sequencing runs deposited in the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) are assigned to the bacterium *Escherichia coli*.  First, the organism name was resolved to its NCBI taxonomy identifier (taxid = 562) using the ncbi_taxonomy_lookup tool, which confirmed one matching taxonomy record.  Second, we queried BRC-Analytics’ federated ENA proxy with brc_ena_runs, requesting a single run (`limit = 1`) solely to retrieve the field `total_in_ena`, the authoritative count of all ENA runs annotated with taxid 562.  The query returned 551 679 runs.  This figure provides a current measure of publicly available *E. coli* sequencing data in ENA and can guide researchers in assessing data availability for comparative genomics, metagenomics, and antimicrobial-resistance studies.

## I. Introduction  
Background.  *Escherichia coli* is a widely studied model organism and an important human pathogen.  Publicly archived *E. coli* sequencing runs enable large-scale analyses of microbial diversity, evolution, and epidemiology.  
Literature Review.  No literature was retrieved for this query.  
Knowledge Gap.  The precise current number of *E. coli* runs in ENA was not specified.  
Objective & Hypothesis.  We aimed to determine the total count of ENA sequencing runs labeled with *E. coli* (taxid 562).  We expected that ENA would catalogue several hundred-thousand runs given the organism’s extensive study history.

## II. Materials and Methods  
Study Design.  A two-step workflow resolved the organism’s taxonomy ID, then used that identifier to query ENA for run counts.  
Materials.  
• NCBI Taxonomy via ncbi_taxonomy_lookup  
• ENA proxy at BRC-Analytics via brc_ena_runs  
Procedures.  
1. ncbi_taxonomy_lookup  
   • proteins: not applicable  
   • query = “Escherichia coli”  
2. brc_ena_runs  
   • taxonomy_id = “562”  
   • limit = 1 (to minimize data transfer)  
   • offset = 0  
   • Retrieved field: `total_in_ena`  
Statistical Analysis.  The run count was taken directly from `total_in_ena`, which ENA reports as the number of runs matching the taxon filter.  No further calculations, deduplication, or percentage derivations were required.

## III. Results  
Data Presentation.  

Table 1. ENA sequencing runs annotated with *Escherichia coli* (taxid = 562).

| Taxonomy ID | Organism            | total_in_ena (runs) |
|-------------|--------------------|---------------------|
| 562         | Escherichia coli   | 551 679             |

Findings.  ENA contains 551 679 sequencing runs assigned to *Escherichia coli* (taxid 562).

## IV. Discussion  
Interpretation.  Over half a million *E. coli* sequencing runs are publicly available in ENA, reflecting the organism’s prominence in microbiology and genomics.  
Context.  This volume of data supports extensive comparative and population-genomic studies, metagenomic analyses, and antimicrobial-resistance surveillance.  
Limitations.  The `total_in_ena` field counts runs annotated with taxid 562; misannotation or absence of taxonomic metadata could lead to minor under- or over-estimation.  The snapshot reflects ENA’s holdings at query time and may change as new data are submitted.  
Conclusion & Future Directions.  With 551 679 runs, researchers have a vast resource for *E. coli* genomic analyses.  Future work could stratify these runs by library strategy, geographic origin, or isolation source to identify data subsets relevant to specific research questions.

## References  
[1] NCBI Taxonomy esearch query for “Escherichia coli”. https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi?term=Escherichia+coli&retmax=50&retstart=0&sort=relevance&retmode=json&db=taxonomy&tool=fdea-ncbi-mcp&email=jonathangunti%40gmail.com  
[2] NCBI Taxonomy efetch for taxid 562. https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/efetch.fcgi?id=562&retmode=xml&db=taxonomy&tool=fdea-ncbi-mcp&email=jonathangunti%40gmail.com  
[3] BRC Analytics ENA proxy query for taxid 562. https://brc-analytics.org/api/v1/ena/taxonomy/562?limit=1  

## Acknowledgments  
We acknowledge the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) for the Taxonomy database and BRC Analytics for providing federated access to ENA run metadata.
